key_claims: In an 8-week overtraining model in mice, dopamine and tyrosine hydroxylase (TyrH) remained elevated in the hippocampus 48 hours after performance testing. A single bout of exhausting exercise increased dopamine shortly after completion. The overtrained mice showed no significant changes in hippocampal serotonin levels. Researchers propose that disrupted dopamine regulation after excessive training may be relevant to symptoms like insomnia, anxiety, and fatigue.
limitations: The study was conducted in mice, and human trials are needed to confirm if similar dopamine disruptions occur in people. The researchers did not directly measure sleep, anxiety, or alertness in the study animals. Surrogate biological markers (such as blood DNA methylation clocks) do not measure tissue-specific botanical, anti-inflammatory, joint, enzymatic, or mucosal benefits.
what_not_to_say: Do not claim that this study proves excessive exercise causes insomnia, anxiety, or fatigue in humans. Do not state that serotonin was elevated or responsible for overtraining fatigue. Do not suggest surrogate clock scores measure tissue-specific botanical, anti-inflammatory, joint, enzymatic, or mucosal benefits.
